title: Starlink: Why Elon Musk is taking on Mukesh Ambani and Jio over satellite internet
source_used: BBC (own reporting, read in full); also read: Al Jazeera/Reuters (8 Oct), The New Indian Express and The Economic Times (PTI/ANI, 9 Oct), Rediff Money (PTI, 8 Oct), Deccan Herald (9 Oct)
key_facts: Musk, who heads SpaceX and Starlink, wrote on X on Wed 7 Oct 2026 that 'certain oligarchs' were blocking Starlink in India to keep a 'monopolistic chokehold' on Indian consumers, calling it 'a crime against the people of India' (BBC; Reuters via Al Jazeera).

On Thu 8 Oct Musk posted that Starlink is licensed in over 165 countries and has spent five years complying with Indian requirements, and asked 'Is Ambani the real boss of India?' (BBC). Mukesh Ambani is chairman of Reliance Industries, owner of Jio, India's biggest mobile operator; the BBC says Ambani and Reliance had not responded.

India's Ministry of Communications said on 8 Oct that Starlink, Eutelsat OneWeb and Jio Satellite Communications are at broadly the same stage, all awaiting security clearances and spectrum allocation, and called the claim of unfairness 'baseless and misconceived' without naming Musk (BBC).

Communications Minister Jyotiraditya Scindia said on Fri 9 Oct that India does not allow a monopoly in any sector, that Jio, OneWeb and Starlink hold licences, that Amazon would have to follow the process, and that a satcom pricing framework is close to being decided (New Indian Express; Economic Times, citing ANI). Minister of State Chandra Sekhar Pemmasani said the matter is pending with the Home Ministry for security clearance.

Rahul Gandhi, Leader of the Opposition in the Lok Sabha, replied to Musk on 8 Oct 'Welcome to India, Elon. Wait till you discover the other guy'; Musk answered 'Thank you, Rahul. This is indeed troubling'. On 9 Oct Gandhi said India needs a level playing field and he is 'anti-monopoly' (PTI via Economic Times).

On 9 Oct BJP leader Ram Madhav said spectrum would be allocated under the law without discrimination and that Jio and Airtel are also waiting; he accused Congress of 'surrendering' to Musk, and said Congress had earlier called Starlink a security threat (PTI via Economic Times). Scindia also took a swipe at Congress.

Reliance Industries shares fell 2.43 percent to Rs 1,177.30 on 8 Oct, a drop of about Rs 39,718 crore in value; PTI linked it to the row, but the Sensex also fell 1.44 percent that day (PTI via Rediff Money).

Deccan Herald reports that Grok, the AI assistant built by SpaceXAI, part of Musk's SpaceX, when asked by an X user on 8 Oct for the disadvantages of allowing Starlink in India, listed national security risks first.
quote_evidence: "The suggestion that the framework or its application is unfair or discriminatory is baseless and misconceived," the ministry said, without naming Musk directly.

Starlink is licensed in over 165 countries and has spent five years complying with every single law and requirement of the government of India, so why still no license? Is Ambani the real boss of India?
"Let me be very clear. India does not allow a monopoly in any sector."
why_it_matters_hint: Starlink cannot sell internet in India until security and spectrum steps are done; Musk blames business interests, the government says all three licensees are treated alike.
event_date: Musk's first post 7 Oct 2026; Ambani post 8 Oct 2026; Scindia and BJP replies 9 Oct 2026
notes: BBC article read in full. Everything about oligarchs/Ambani is Musk's claim; government rejects it; Reliance had not responded when BBC wrote (Akash Ambani, chairman of Reliance Jio Infocomm, declined to comment at India Mobile Congress, saying 'We want to be heads down and deliver value to our Indian consumers'). CNBC, Telegraph India (access denied) and Bloomberg (bot wall) could not be opened; Reuters read via Al Jazeera. TechCrunch, The Hindu, Indian Express, Forbes, Business Insider and Free Press Journal not opened; Grok item taken from Deccan Herald.
